messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 streaming latency spike detected for customer Sapphire (single-tenant). Region: us-west-2. p95 ~ 450ms -> p99 ~ 3.2s, streaming stalls reported. SLO breached. Paging on-call. root_ts=2765432100
Amber Cheng: picking this up — I'm oncall. grabbing context now.
Amber Cheng: @ryan can you confirm whether model variant fallback was triggered? customer using gptx-13b-highmem pinned?
Ryan Liu: saw the alert, brb with logs. Not seeing automatic fallback triggered in the router logs. Requests are queuing on the streaming mux layer.
Amber Cheng: ok starting live triage: impact = Sapphire prod (single-tenant), ~120 concurrent streams, ~12% streaming half-closed/stall after first chunk.
Maya Patel: FYI Sapphire CS on standby, they're seeing degraded UX (spinning responses). They're asking for ETA.
Amber Cheng: immediate mitigation options: 1) scale dedicated pool (add 2 nodes), 2) enable fallback to quantized gptx-13b-q4 on routing, 3) apply short-term per-tenant concurrency cap. Trying #1 now.
ops-sre: scaling dedicated pool nodes in us-west-2. Running kubectl scale --replicas=6 ds/redwood-infer-gpu-sapphire-usw2
infra-bot: [action] scale request queued -> rolling up new nodes, expected ready ~90s.
Jason Ortiz: quick check — do we have KV cache hotpath thrash? long prefix fanout? Can we see token distribution for these sessions?
Ryan Liu: pulling KV cache metrics: suspicious high misses on shard 7, eviction spikes coincident with the surge. Looks like some sessions are sending very long prefixes ~4-6k tokens which bypass prefix caching.
Amber Cheng: that matches customer report — they batch user history into a single prompt. Long prefix + streaming = high memory + serialization costs.
Maya Patel: customer is open to temporary throttling on long-prefix requests if it reduces impact.
Amber Cheng: applying per-tenant prefix-length throttle: router flag prefix_max_tokens=3000 for Sapphire. Pushing config now: curl -X POST https://config.redwood.internal/tenants/sapphire -d '{"prefix_max_tokens":3000}'
infra-bot: config update accepted, applying to routing nodes.
Amber Cheng: enabling model fallback on router: allow_model_fallback=true for Sapphire, fallback_model=gptx-13b-q4. Doing a dry-run first.
Ryan Liu: dry-run shows ~18% of inflight requests eligible for fallback (latency-sensitive streaming). If we enable forced fallback we should see immediate p99 drop but risk of slightly different outputs. recommend enable with notify to customer.
Maya Patel: I'll notify Sapphire that we may fall back to a quantized variant for stability, will ask permission to proceed.
support-bot: Sapphire support ticket #SAPP-44221 created and linked to incident.
Amber Cheng: second mitigation: enable short-circuit streaming chunk size to reduce backpressure: set streaming_chunk_bytes=8k (was 32k) on gateway. Pushing now.
ops-sre: gateway config patched via helm upgrade, rolling restart of ingress pods.
Amber Cheng: scale completed — new nodes ready. Monitoring p95/p99.
infra-bot: new worker nodes registered (2). Pool capacity +40%.
Ryan Liu: initial telemetry after scale + chunk change looks better: p95 ~ 160ms, p99 ~ 1.1s (improved), but we still see intermittent stalls when some sessions hit long prefixes.
Maya Patel: Sapphire approved fallback to quantized for 10 minutes while they investigate prompt size. Proceed.
Amber Cheng: enabling fallback now (force) — routing flag set.
Jason Ortiz: routing shows ~22% of streams now on gptx-13b-q4. CPU/GPU utilization normalized.
Ryan Liu: p99 dipped to ~520ms after fallback. Streaming stalls largely gone.
Amber Cheng: marking immediate customer impact mitigated. Still keeping page open for postmortem.
Maya Patel: I'm sending a short note to Sapphire: "We've enabled a temporary model fallback and adjusted streaming chunking; these steps should restore responsiveness. Please review prompt batching patterns and consider trimming or using the embeddings cache."
Amber Cheng: follow-ups: 1) postmortem to root cause: prefix fanout + KV cache evictions + insufficient routing fallback behavior, 2) investigate why automatic fallback didn't trigger earlier, 3) improve alerting threshold to detect long-prefix-induced cache thrash, 4) provide tenant-level throttle knobs to CS.
Ryan Liu: grabbing diagnostic bundle and kube logs for the window 2765432000-2765432350. Pasting commands: ```
# gather logs
kubectl logs -l app=router -n infra --since=10m > /tmp/router_logs_2765432100.log
redis-cli --latency -h kvcache-7.usw2 > /tmp/kvcache_latency_2765432100.log
```
Amber Cheng: posting a short incident summary to #incidents once we close. Also will create a runbook item to detect long-prefix surges.
Jason Ortiz: small runtime fix idea — make fallback eligibility check include prefix token count so we auto-fallback earlier when prefix > 2k. Filing a ticket.
ops-sre: any lingering customer-visible errors?
Maya Patel: Sapphire reports UX restored, no further complaints. Closing customer escalation.
Amber Cheng: thanks team. We'll keep the thread open for 2 hours for any regressions, then transition to a postmortem PR.
incident-bot: Incident 2026-03-15T22:35:00Z created: sapphire-streaming-buffer-wave. Severity: P2. Assigned: Amber Cheng.
support-bot: Linked support ticket #SAPP-44221 -> incident 2765432100.
Amber Cheng: draft notes for postmortem: cause hypothesis, timeline, mitigations, action items (auto-fallback criteria, prefix throttles, cache shard rebalancing, runtime config defaults). I'll put the draft in docs/incidents/2765432100-sapphire-draft.md in 30m.
Ryan Liu: uploading diagnostic bundle to s3://incidents/2765432100/bundle.tar.gz.
Amber Cheng: wrapping up — final p99 at 490ms, p95 150ms. Closing active paging. We'll schedule a follow-up with Sapphire CS tomorrow to review prompt patterns and quota options. :thumbsup:
Maya Patel: thanks everyone.
Jason Ortiz: good job.
ops-sre: closing action items in ops board, will follow up on pool autoscale tuning.
incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (no active SLO breach).
